{{Quote|Your buddy here was about to be turned into orange goo. He picked a fight with a Dug, an especially dangerous Dug called Sebulba&hellip;|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], about [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]|<ref name="Episode 1">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
'''Dugs''' were an aggressive [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] that used their upper [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] for locomotion and their lower limbs for grappling.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Dug_Modder_SM.png|thumb|left|150px|A Dug mechanic modifying a blaster]]
Dugs were slender, powerfully built beings with a somewhat [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] build and a unique method of walking that hailed from the high gravity world [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]]. Their primary means of locomotion were their strong arms, and their lower limbs and feet were used for grappling and other fine motor manipulation. They hardly ever walked on their lower limbs. [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]] was only once seen standing on his legs. Although most Dugs may walk on all four limbs, others liked to use their strong arms as legs and their feet as hands like they would normally do.<ref name="Gran in the Databank">{{DB|species|gran|Gran}}</ref><ref name="TEGTAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref><ref name="TNEGTAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>

Dugs had smooth skin, which hung loosely around their tall necks, only to inflate during mating season calls. They also possessed fin-like ears and pronounced snouts. They lived mainly in the forests of the [[Malastare's western continent|western continent]] of their homeworld in primitive tree villages called "[[tree thorp]]s". On their homeworld Malastare, the Dugs were arboreal beings. They brachiated among the canopies at high speed using all four limbs.<ref name="Gran in the Databank" /><ref name="TEGTAS" /><ref name="TNEGTAS" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Dugs insult everybody. You know that. You shouldn't value their words.|[[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to a [[Barabel/Legends|Barabel]]|<ref name="TEGTAS" />}}
Due to their oppression under their [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] rulers who colonized Malastare, many Dugs often felt the need to throw around their strength in bids to establish dominance. As a result, they were known for their ill-tempered demeanor, and many were bullying thugs.

<div style="float:right">[[File:Dug_warriors.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Dug cavalier/Legends|Dug cavaliers]] during the [[Battle of Malastare/Legends|Battle of Malastare]]]]</div>
On their homeworld of Malastare, the vast majority of Dugs were little more than laborers toiling for the enrichment of the Gran. With the species excluded from much of the power and money on Malastare, many Dugs, such as Sebulba, turned to [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] as their only means to achieve fame and fortune. In all other areas, the Dugs were exploited and disenfranchised.

Dug mating is very reminiscent of some reptiles, which may indicate their ancestry. The loose folds of skin around the [[Gender/Legends|males]] neck inflated during the mating season, showing a display of color. An interested female may pester or disturb a male in a few different ways until his balloon-neck deflates with a screech. After this, the two are considered mated. Mates remain loyal to each other, even though they may bully each other through their time together.

Because of their experiences with the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]], the Dugs were [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] and rarely left their homeworld. If they were seen off-planet, they were often seen in groups of their own kind. Most Dugs in the galaxy were criminals or risk-takers, leading many Dugs into podracing and gambling.

==History==
{{Quote|Motivating the Dugs to fight is not difficult, for at the core of their beings are knots of unfocused rage. However, that rage is not centered in the true warrior's drive of hatred, but in insecurity. They are valueless, and they know this. That is why they will always be defeated.|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="TEGTAS" />}}
[[File:Sebulba-2024Base.png|thumb|left|200px|[[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]], a notorious Dug [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]].]]
In ancient times, the Dugs were first to fight for their lives against the massive [[Zillo Beast/Legends|Zillo Beasts]], which were their primary predators. However, they eventually managed to use the planet's [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]] reserves to kill off all but one of the creatures, which would remain hibernating underground for thousands of years.<ref name="ZilloBeast" />

Circa [[8000 BBY]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] established an outpost on Malastare since it was located at a key spot along the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] trade route. Later, in ca. [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], a contingent of [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] colonists settled on the planet. First contact between the Gran and the Dugs was bloody, and a long, brutal [[Dug-Gran conflict|war]] ensued.<ref name="Gran in the Databank" />

[[File:Sebulba-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|150px]]
Because of the power and influence the Gran wielded in the Galactic Senate, the Republic [[Gran Protectorate Act/Legends|settled]] the violence in the Grans' favor. The [[Gran Protectorate/Legends|Gran Protectorate]] was established and Dugs were demilitarized, stripped of political power, and relocated to the [[Malastare's western continent|western continent]] of their own planet. The Gran ruled Malastare and represented the planet in the Galactic Senate. Dugs were little more than subservient laborers treated as slaves and paid minute wages.<ref name="Gran in the Databank" /> An organization called [[Dugs-for-Democracy]] protested against this treatment and would go on to oppose the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]].<ref name="HNNV.531 55">[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 55|''HoloNet News Vol. 531'' #55]]</ref>

During the [[Battle of Malastare/Legends|Battle of Malastare]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Separatists deployed a large droid army that outnumbered the local Dug and Republic defenders. In response, Republic forces deployed a new [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], the [[Electro-proton bomb/Legends|electro-proton bomb]], which quickly obliterated the droid forces but awakened the planet's last surviving Zillo Beast. The Zillo Beast devastated the Republic and Dug lines, resulting in heavy losses. [[Doge/Legends|Doge]] [[Nakha Urus/Legends|Nakha Urus]], the leader of the Dugs, and his comrades demanded that the Republic destroy the beast, in exchange for signing the [[Treaty of Malastare/Legends|Treaty of Malastare]], giving the Republic access to Malastare's fuel supplies. However, rather than killing it outright, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Skywalker]] secretly planned for the beast to be stunned in order to obtain its hide for scientific research while appeasing the Dugs. The Zillo Beast was stunned using Republic [[RX-200 Falchion-class assault tank/Legends|stun tanks]], and the beast was transported to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] for controlled research.<ref name="ZilloBeast" /> However shortly after arrival, the Zillo Beast escaped and proceeded to wreak havoc, endangering the lives of millions and forcing the Jedi to eliminate it.<ref name="IGN">{{WebCite|url=http://tv.ign.com/objects/067/067069.html|text=IGN Episode Guide|archivedate=20100411235214}}</ref>

Under the New Republic, a [[Unidentified New Republic Dug diplomat|Dug diplomat]] lived on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="TWOFSW:AFG">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> By the time of the [[Second Imperial Civil War]] in [[137 ABY]], at least one Dug, [[Andurgo]], served as a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] pilot in the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]]'s [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], which saw extensive service.<ref name="SWL47">[[Legacy (2006) 47|''Legacy'' (2006) 47]]</ref>
